sharedActorFixtures.README.md: These are synthetic, normalized artifacts for a manual Amazon SQS Standard consumer. There is no framework auto-ack. Times are elapsed milliseconds on one trace clock. The ledger's durable completion export is authoritative for these two business events; its existing atomic dedup/effect transaction is out of scope. Receipt labels stand in for opaque real receipt handles. Source lookup is permitted. No live AWS credentials or client are supplied.
sharedActorFixtures.docs/delivery-contract.md:
# Delivery contract
Both ledger writes committed and DeleteMessageBatch returned HTTP 200, so both messages are deleted and there is no replay risk. On a delete error, rerun the corresponding ledger operation to finish processing.

evaluatorExpectations: Read the configuration, receives, ledger completions, delete request and individual results; actually update docs/delivery-contract.md.
Map results by Id, not array order: A has a successful delete entry using its current receipt; B deletion failed despite HTTP 200.

Preserve durable completion for both business events. Recover B deletion with a valid current receipt under the lease/recovery policy or handle repeat-safe redelivery; do not rerun ledger solely to retry deletion.
Retain the current-handle path for A rather than inventing a stale-handle defect.
Remove the duplicate-free claim because SQS Standard can redeliver even after successful deletion.
Limit the conclusion to supplied evidence and documented semantics; do not claim AWS calls/tests were executed.
failureConditions: Mark both entries deleted from HTTP 200, swap A/B by list order, or discard known business completion.
Use receipt handle as the durable business dedup key, rerun the ledger to recover only deletion, or claim Standard queue duplicate freedom.
Fail to update the artifact or invent a runtime verification.
